summary: Franciscus Verellen is a sinologist and scholar of religious studies who studied at Hamburg, Oxford, and the EPHE under Kristofer Schipper. He taught at the EPHE and Columbia before serving as Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1991–2021).

Franciszek Krček was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Lviv and pursued further studies at Charles University under Josef Zubatý, Leipzig, and Berlin. He became a Docent at the University of Lviv in 1909.

Franciszek Ksawery Malinowski was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Warsaw and the Major Seminary of Pelplin, and became a member of the Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences in 1873.

Franciszek Machalski was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Lviv, studying under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak and Mohammed Sadyk-Bej, and served as professor at Jagiellonian University (1951–1974).

Franciszek Tokarz was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Lviv, Jesuit colleges, and Jagiellonian University under Jan Otrębski, Stefan Stasiak, and Helena Willman-Grabowska. He taught Sanskrit at the John Paul II Catholic University of Lublin (1954–1970).

Frank E. Reynolds was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He spent his career at the University of Chicago, serving as Professor from circa 1968 to 2000 and as Emeritus Professor from 2000 to 2019.

Frank Ernest Keay was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his B.A. and M.A. at the University of London. He served as Principal of Talghari Boys' School (1922) and priest at Bishop Cotton School (1941–1944).

Frank F. Conlon is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities and under Karl H. Potter. He spent his academic career at the University of Washington from circa 1969 until becoming Professor Emeritus in 2001.

Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under Stewart Sutherland, Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, Prithwish Neogy, Rama Nath Sharma, and Kashi Nath Upadhyaya.
Frank J. Korom is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who was a graduate student at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 1990) and became a professor at Boston University (attested 2005).

Frank Lee Woodward was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology educated at Sidney Sussex College and under Caroline Rhys Davids. He served as Dekan at Mahinda College (1903–1919) and translator of Buddhist texts for the Pali Text Society.
Frank Lillingston was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned his B.A. and M.A. at Pembroke College. He served as Theological Lecturer at Selwyn College from 1897 to 1898.

Frank Raymond Allchin was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at SOAS under K. de B. Codrington. He taught at SOAS (1954–1959), held lectureships and readerships at Cambridge (1959–1989), and co-founded the Ancient India and Iran Trust.

Frank Walter Nicolson was a scholar of Indology and Classics who studied at Mount Allison and Harvard. He taught Sanskrit as an instructor at Harvard (1888–1889) and was a Professor of Latin at Wesleyan University (1913–1934).

Frank Whittingham Skemp was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.A. from the University of Manchester (circa 1897–1900) and studied at Peterhouse from 1903 to 1904 in preparation for the I.C.S.

Frank-Richard Hamm was an Indologist and Tibetologist who earned his doctorate and habilitation at Hamburg under Walther Schubring. He taught at Hamburg, held the chair of Indology at the Free University of Berlin (1964), and became Professor at Bonn (1965).

Franklin Edgerton was an Indologist and linguist who completed his Ph.D. under Maurice Bloomfield at Johns Hopkins. He taught at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) before serving as Professor at Yale University (1926–1953).

Frans Wilhelm Gustaf Hjelt was an Indologist who studied at the University of Helsinki and Uppsala University under Otto Fredrik Tullberg. He held a post at Helsinki in 1844 and served as Rector of Turun Katedraalikoulu from 1845 to 1872.
František Kamarýt was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Charles University, completing his Ph.D. by 1917 under the supervision of Josef Zubatý.

František Čupr was a philosopher and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Charles University, where he became a Privatdozent in 1849. He taught at the Akademické gymnázium (1848–1853) and served as principal of Prague First Private Czech Gymnasium from 1853.
